1980: WHEN LESTER HAYES TOOK OVER THE NFL

There have been dominant seasons in NFL history. Quarterbacks have bent the league. Pass rushers have terrorized it. Running backs have carried it.

But only once has a cornerback controlled an entire NFL season the way Lester Hayes did in 1980.

That year remains one of the most dominant single seasons ever produced by a defensive back - not because of one statistic, but because of how completely he changed the behavior of offenses.

Hayes intercepted 13 passes in a 16-game regular season. That number alone commands attention. But it’s what followed that defines dominance.

In the postseason he added five more interceptions. He finished the year as NFL Defensive Player of the Year, First-Team All-Pro, and a Super Bowl Champion.

No defensive back before or since has combined league-leading takeaways, postseason control, and a championship run in a single season quite like this.

Hayes coverage style was confrontational and suffocating. He disrupted timing at the line, rode receivers through their stems, and attacked the football like it belonged to him. 

His effectiveness was so overwhelming that the league eventually banned Stickum, because one defender had pushed competitive balance too far.

Hayes remained a Pro Bowl level player after the ban. What changed most was the willingness of quarterbacks to challenge him at all.

Many corners have been great. Some have been smoother. A few have been longer, faster, or more technically pristine. But none have owned a year the way Lester Hayes owned 1980.

That season wasn’t just the best year by a cornerback. It was one of the most dominant seasons by any defensive player in NFL history regardless of position.

For one unforgettable year, the most influential player in professional football didn’t touch the ball on offense. He waited for it. And when quarterbacks forgot who he was, he reminded them.

1980 didn’t belong to an offense. It belonged to Lester Hayes.

TL;DR 🏎️ Can the Tesla Roadster really hit 400 mph? 

✅ A 0-60 time under one second is believable. The thrusters push with about 4x the car’s own weight, so the physics checks out.

✅ A 230 mph top speed is easy, since it takes only about 700 hp.

🌙 A 400 mph peak is a moonshot, but it isn’t fantasy. 

Holding 400 mph on electric power alone would take over 3,000 hp, likely more than any production car has ever made. The trick is the cold-gas thrusters. They only last about 2 seconds, but in that burst they could add 110 to 170 mph. If the car starts near 300 mph, a brief touch of 400 is possible on paper.

There’s a catch, though: no road tire has ever been proven at 400 mph, and at that speed the air tries to lift the car off the ground.

The history of guitar speakers is inseparable from the amplifiers that housed them. Jensen, Celestion, Altec Lansing, Electro-Voice and Eminence supplied factory-standard drivers, custom OEM designs and optional upgrades. Those choices shaped amplifier response.
